column3: Joins the heavens and earth to their continual praise and closes with the same forbearance and forgiveness.
Paradise adornment does not clarify cosmic preservation or the closing attributes.
Its holding of a child against burial is a distant and ethically contrasting use of holding.
Divine knowledge of what is hidden in heavens and earth frames forgiveness as informed rather than powerless.
Affirms that nothing in heavens or earth can frustrate divine power, supporting the focus's exclusive cosmic agency.
Forgiveness and forbearance recur, but its charitable-exchange setting adds little after the closer attribute parallel.
Directly depicts God holding the sky from falling upon the earth, a concrete parallel to the focus's preservation.
The description of paradise ornaments adds no relevant relation.
Birds held aloft supply a visible, creature-scale instance of the sustaining action.
Creation of heavens and earth establishes the creator's authority behind their continued preservation.
The demand for ornaments and angels does not illuminate the focus.
Forbearance in inheritance law gives only a remote ethical setting for the closing attribute.
No one can withhold what God releases or release what He withholds, sharply expressing exclusive control after Him.
Knowledge of the unseen heavens, earth, and inner selves supports the focus's non-arbitrary forbearance.
Confinement is an unrelated and punitive use of holding.
Abraham's forbearance retains compassion while recognizing a decisive boundary, adding an ethical dimension to hilm.
God's dominion over heavens and earth grounds the sole authority implicit in their preservation.
Forgiving restraint in leaving some matters undisclosed offers a distinct form of protective forbearance.
Forgiveness and mercy appear without a specific relation to sustaining or restraining the cosmos.
The immediate context denies alleged partners any share in creating earth or heavens, clarifying why none can hold them after God.
The wrongdoers' claim that they would never pass away contrasts false assumed permanence with the focus's dependent stability.
The command to seek forgiveness adds only the already represented forgiveness theme.
Comprehensive recording of what is hidden in heavens and earth only indirectly supports informed preservation.
Its image of mountains being removed supplies a counterpoint to the focus's prevention of cosmic displacement.
Withering crops and disbelief do not add a usable connection.
The inheritance of scripture and differing recipients do not clarify the focus.
A forgiving Lord in the account of a settled land offers only a distant contextual echo.
Calling attention to the dominion of heavens and earth broadens the focus into reflective recognition of created order.
Birds sustained in the open sky furnish another concrete sign of continuous divine holding.
Human arrogance and judgment add no relevant relation.
It denies that rivals can avert harm or hold back mercy, reinforcing exclusive power to withhold or preserve.
Revelation's truthfulness does not add a direct link to the focus.
The description of a forbearing son gives only a limited human echo of hilm.
Fear of punishment and allegiance to Satan do not clarify the focus.
Creation of heavens and earth with purpose resists treating their maintained order as aimless.
Cosmic alternation and forgiveness provide a distant, already-covered stability and mercy parallel.
Forbearance in judging unintentional oaths is an ethical analogue rather than a cosmic one.
The warning of seizure adds a local consequence but little beyond the adjacent power context.
Its prohibition on harmful marital retention gives a contrasting ethical limit on human holding.
Ritual concession and forgiveness only remotely reflect protective restraint.
This repeats purposeful creation without adding to the prior creation-and-order parallel.
Holding fast to revelation supplies a normative analogue to stability maintained against deviation.
Knowledge of hearts and forbearance remain confined to a social arrangement.
Forgiveness removing sorrow and grateful reward add the focus's mercy side within its immediate surah context.
Rightful retention or release in divorce is a limited ethical analogue to holding.
The Creator of heavens and earth couples forgiveness with delay to an appointed term, clarifying forbearance as deliberate respite.
The source of revelation does not materially illuminate the focus.
Holding fast to inherited authority contrasts a false human attachment with a sound basis for commitment.
Withdrawal of mercy shows dependence on divine giving but lacks the focus's preservation theme.
It contrasts the destructive covering of disbelief with forgiveness that protects from consequence.
The unbreakable handhold offers a metaphor of stability, but not the focus's cosmic action.
Human pride after relief adds no relevant relation.
The golden calf episode does not clarify sustaining power or forbearance.
Knowing and forbearing treatment of the harmed offers only a general ethical parallel.
The rhetorical question about belief adds no usable connection.
Forgiveness and gratitude repeat the local mercy theme without explaining cosmic preservation.
Retaining hunted prey is an unrelated practical use of holding.
Household boundaries and disclosure do not clarify the focus.
Exclusive knowledge of the unseen in heavens and earth supports the divine knowledge underlying unshared governance.
Forgiveness and reward provide a redundant moral-outcome parallel.
The rescue and impending punishment do not add to the focus.
Divine delay despite human wrongdoing explains forbearance as restraint and shows how judgment is held back to an appointed term.
Forgiveness preserves Moses from ultimate consequence without erasing responsibility, adding a concrete mercy dimension.
Divine oneness supports sole agency but is too compressed to add much after the explicit exclusivity cards.
The prophetic covenant does not clarify the focus.
Control over giving or withholding a gift is a distant analogue of divine retention.
The wordplay around musk does not provide a meaningful relation.
The inability of invoked others to hear or answer reinforces the focus's claim that no one else can sustain what God holds.
Shared prayer for forgiveness and mercy adds a redundant interpersonal protection theme.
Unmatched punishment does not illuminate preservation or forbearance.
Accountability for truthfulness does not add a relevant connection.
The forgiving and loving attributes repeat the mercy theme without the focus's sustaining action.
Ownership of heavens and earth supplies a broad but already represented sovereignty basis.
The parable of what remains versus what passes away gives only an indirect image of enduring order.
The paired request for forgiveness and protection from the Fire makes mercy explicitly protective.
Heavens nearly splitting above while angels seek forgiveness for earth joins cosmic instability directly to mercy and forgiveness.
The polemical reference to adornment does not clarify the focus.
Holding souls at death and releasing others until an appointed term gives a close account of deliberate holding and release.
Dominion over heavens and earth joined to forgiving or punishing relates sovereign cosmic rule to mercy.
A near repetition of cosmic ownership and forgiveness adds little after the fuller parallel.
The Creator of heavens and earth can remove people and bring new creation, making their persistence visibly contingent.
Withholding provision shows that divine holding can preserve or deprive according to what is retained.
It says the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted if truth followed human desire, stressing order's dependence on divine constraint.
Prayer for an erring father adds a limited ethical instance of forgiveness.
God's dominion over heavens and earth, life, and death establishes Him as the sole protector and helper.
Lordship over heavens and earth with forgiveness restates themes already supplied more specifically.
Rain reviving earth shows beneficent power but not the distinctive holding or restraint at issue.
Seeking forgiveness after affirming divine oneness is a redundant moral response.
Measured provision prevents corruption, presenting restraint as knowledgeable preservation rather than lack of power.
The promise of forgiveness and reward repeats the mercy theme without a further connection.
Universal ownership supports sovereignty but adds little after multiple closer ownership statements.
The angels' plea distinguishes forgiveness of past burden from protection against coming punishment.
Forgiveness and mercy accompany migration but do not clarify cosmic preservation.
Human forgiveness preventing retaliatory harm is a distant, redundant ethical analogue.
The denial of water and provision in the hereafter does not add a relevant link.
Seeking forgiveness for believers gives a general communal mercy parallel.
The assessment of desert dwellers does not clarify the focus.
Forgiveness followed by honor shows restorative mercy but is redundant at this rank.
The reference to earlier prophets adds no usable relation.
Knowledge of inner selves joined to forgiveness for those who return offers a late, general mercy parallel.
It explicitly joins divine knowledge with forgiveness and forbearance, adding an ethical instance of the focus's closing attributes.
God's throne encompasses the heavens and earth, and preserving them does not tire Him, making this the closest direct parallel.
After failure, God forgives and is explicitly forgiving and forbearing, directly developing the focus's final attributes.
Creation of heavens and earth and their alternating order directs reflection toward a coherent, maintained cosmos.
The Originator of heavens and earth, who knows everything, supplies a creation-and-knowledge basis for their preservation.
The Creator who established authority and directs every affair presents cosmic order as continuously governed.
God raises the heavens without visible pillars and subjects the celestial bodies, directly portraying upheld and ordered heaven.
The creator of heavens and earth can recreate humanity, stressing that created existence remains contingent on divine power.
The joining and separation of heavens and earth places their present order within an active divine origination.
The sky is made a protected canopy, a close parallel to divine preservation above the earth.
The ordered courses of night, day, sun, and moon provide a concrete pattern of sustained celestial governance.
Rolling up the heaven at the appointed end shows that its continuance and cessation rest wholly with God.
Creation of heavens and earth in truth grounds their order in purposeful divine action.
Heaven and earth standing by God's command is an especially direct formulation of the focus's sustaining claim.
Heavens without visible pillars and mountains set to keep earth from shaking closely portray the restraint of cosmic instability.
The possibility of earth swallowing people or fragments of heaven falling makes present cosmic security visibly dependent on divine restraint.
The distinct ordered courses of sun, moon, night, and day present celestial stability as governed rather than self-sustaining.
Earth held in God's grasp and the heavens folded by Him give an emphatic image of complete cosmic sovereignty.
The greater creation of heavens and earth relativizes human power and reinforces the scale of divine sustaining capacity.
The raised, adorned sky without fissures offers an observable sign of ordered and preserved structure.
The heaven built with divine power broadens the focus's sustaining action to its deliberate cosmic construction.
Raising the heaven and setting the balance portrays order as an established and maintained divine measure.
Sovereignty over heavens and earth, together with life and death, reinforces the focus's exclusive agency.
The layered heavens and descending command present the cosmos as governed throughout by divine decree.
The layered heavens are made without visible inconsistency, supplying a sign of sustained cosmic coherence.
The construction of seven firm heavens adds a compact image of stable celestial structure.
The heaven's raised roof and ordered formation present it as deliberately fashioned rather than autonomous.
